He is a two-time [[NBA All-Star Game|NBA All-Star]], and earned [[NBA All-Defensive Team|NBA All-Defensive Second Team]] honors in 2014 with the [[Indiana Pacers]]. Hibbert was the runner-up for the [[NBA Defensive Player of the Year Award]] in the [[2013–14 NBA season]], placing second behind [[Joakim Noah]].{{cite web|url=https://www.indycornrows.com/2014/4/21/5638404/joakim-noah-wins-nba-defensive-player-of-the-year-roy-hibbert|title=Joakim Noah wins NBA Defensive Player of the Year, Hibbert places second, Paul George seventh|first=Tom|last=Lewis|date=April 21, 2014|access-date=July 12, 2020|archive-date=November 8, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221108045548/https://www.indycornrows.com/2014/4/21/5638404/joakim-noah-wins-nba-defensive-player-of-the-year-roy-hibbert|url-status=dead}} Hibbert played [[college basketball]] for the [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown Hoyas]] and was named a consensus second-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] as a senior in 2008. He was drafted 17th overall in the [[2008 NBA draft]] by the [[Toronto Raptors]] and was subsequently traded to the Indiana Pacers on draft night. Hibbert has represented the [[Jamaica national basketball team|Jamaica national team]] in international competition, being eligible because of his dual U.S. and Jamaican citizenship.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/web_100727.html|title=After brief setback, Sherbert back to work|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|date=July 27, 2010|access-date=May 24, 2013}}{{cite web|url=https://nba.nbcsports.com/2013/10/04/roy-hibberts-chance-of-joining-usa-basketball-appears-to-be-a-long-shot/|title=Roy Hibbert's chance of joining USA Basketball appears to be a long shot|first=Brett|last=Pollakoff|date=October 5, 2013}} ==Early life== Hibbert was born in [[Queens]], New York City to Roy Sr. and Patty Hibbert. His father is originally from [[Jamaica]] and his mother from [[Trinidad]]. The family moved to [[Adelphi, Maryland]], when Roy was two. Around that time, the ''[[New York Post]]'' states, his parents introduced him to basketball after they had "tried to get him to play [[tennis]], then [[golf]], then the [[piano]]".Lenn Robbins, [http://www.nypost.com/seven/03112007/sports/biggest_big_man_sports_lenn_robbins.htm?page=0 Biggest Big Man: Hibbert Powers Hoyas to Crown"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070929121045/http://www.nypost.com/seven/03112007/sports/biggest_big_man_sports_lenn_robbins.htm?page=0 |date=September 29, 2007 }}, ''New York Post'', March 11, 2007. ==College career== [[File:Roy Hibbert in 2006.jpg|thumb|Hibbert with the [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown Hoyas]] in December 2006]] Hibbert was named to the All-Big East Second Team in 2006 along with teammate [[Jeff Green (basketball)|Jeff Green]].[https://www.espn.com/espn/print?id=2356272&type=story Four unanimous selections to all-Big East first team] March 6, 2006 In 2007, he and Green were unanimous selections to the All-Big East First Team, with Green earning Big East Player of the Year honors. The two led the Hoyas to victory in the 2007 Big East Conference Championship for the first time since 1989 against the [[Pittsburgh Panthers basketball|Pittsburgh Panthers]]; Hibbert contributed a double-double with 18 points and 11 rebounds.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=270690046|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170316024830/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=270690046|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 16, 2017|title=Pittsburgh vs. Georgetown - Game Recap - March 10, 2007 - ESPN|website=ESPN.com}} Before the 2007–08 season he was named Big East's preseason player of the year.{{cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/preview?gameId=273140046 |date=November 10, 2007 |title=William & Mary-Georgetown Preview |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=June 2, 2008}} He was also named a pre-season All-American along with the likes of [[Tyler Hansbrough]], whose [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina Tar Heels]] were upset by Hibbert's Hoyas in the Elite Eight of the 2007 NCAA Tournament. Hibbert had repeatedly said that he planned to play all four years and graduate from Georgetown,{{cite web |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2007/04/13/AR2007041301644.html |title=Hoyas' Green, Hibbert Declare for NBA Draft |date=2007-04-13 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |access-date=2022-04-04}} continuing the tradition of graduating Hoya centers such as [[Patrick Ewing]], [[Alonzo Mourning]] and [[Dikembe Mutombo]]. However, his performance in helping to lead the Hoyas to the 2007 Final Four catapulted him into lottery pick status. Hibbert declared his eligibility for the [[2007 NBA draft]], but did not sign with an agent. On May 23, 2007, Hibbert announced he would return to school for his senior season. Hibbert said of Georgetown, "My heart was here. ... I feel like I have unfinished business here."{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/espn/wire/_/section/ncb/id/2880367 |title=Georgetown's Green remains in draft, Hibbert to return to school |website=ESPN.com}} Following the Hoyas' upset loss to Davidson and [[Stephen Curry]] in the second round of the 2008 NCAA Tournament, Hibbert's collegiate career came to a close. In college, Hibbert was often referred to as the "Big Stiff" by reporters and fans.{{cite web|url=http://www.nuvo.net/indianapolis/roy-hibbert-the-pacers-center-of-balance/Content?oid=2441738|title=Roy Hibbert: The Pacers' center of balance|date=April 25, 2012 }}[https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2006/03/18/AR2006031801309.html Hibbert's Starting to Grow on the Hoyas] ==Professional career== ===Indiana Pacers (2008–2015)=== [[File:Roy Hibbert posts up Marcin Gortat.jpg|thumb|Hibbert [[Basketball moves#Shots|posts up]] [[Marcin Gortat]] in February 2011]] [[File:Joakim Noah vs. Roy Hibbert.jpg|thumb|Hibbert battling [[Joakim Noah]] of the [[Chicago Bulls]] for position in December 2011]] [[File:Kris Humphries Donald Sloan.jpg|thumb|Hibbert with the [[Indiana Pacers]] in November 2014]] Hibbert was drafted 17th overall by the [[Toronto Raptors]] in the [[2008 NBA draft]]. On July 9, 2008, his rights were traded to the [[Indiana Pacers]], along with [[T. J. Ford]], for [[Jermaine O'Neal]].{{cite web |title=Pacers announce two trades; acquire seven players |url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers_trades_release_080709.html |website=NBA.com |access-date=February 3, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080712162336/https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers_trades_release_080709.html |archive-date=July 12, 2008 |date=July 9, 2008}} On July 15, he signed his first professional contract with the Pacers.{{citation needed|date=February 2024}} Hibbert was selected to the [[2012 NBA All-Star Game]] as a reserve for the [[Eastern Conference (NBA)|East]]. He played 10 minutes and scored three points, going 1–3 from the field. In Game 1 of the first round of the [[2012 NBA playoffs]] against the [[Orlando Magic]], Hibbert recorded nine blocks. On July 13, 2012, Hibbert re-signed with the Pacers on a reported four-year, $58 million contract, matching the offer sheet from the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/8164675|title=Busy Pacers re-sign center Hibbert, guard Hill|date=July 13, 2012|website=ESPN.com}} On November 21, 2012, Hibbert set a career-high by recording 11 blocks as part of a 10-point, 11-rebound, 11-block [[triple-double]] in a victory against the [[New Orleans Pelicans|New Orleans Hornets]]. His 11 blocks also broke the franchise record for most blocks in a single game, and Hibbert became only the second player in Pacers history (alongside [[Jermaine O'Neal]]) to record a points-rebounds-blocks triple-double. In Game 3 of a [[2013 NBA playoffs|2013 Eastern Conference Semifinals]] series against the [[New York Knicks]], Hibbert recorded 24 points and 12 rebounds in a Pacers win.{{cite web |title=Roy Hibbert takes control as Pacers rough up Knicks |website=[[USA Today]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220128060336/https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/2013/05/11/new-york-knicks-indiana-pacers-playoffs-game-3-score/2153061/ |archive-date=2022-01-28 |url-status=live |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/2013/05/11/new-york-knicks-indiana-pacers-playoffs-game-3-score/2153061/}} In Game 6, Hibbert recorded 25 points and 12 rebounds, along with five blocks,{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=400464469|title=Knicks vs. Pacers - Box Score - May 18, 2013 - ESPN|website=ESPN.com}} including a significant block on [[Carmelo Anthony]], which led the Pacers to the 2013 [[NBA Conference Finals|Eastern Conference Finals]]. Hibbert averaged 15.8 points and 3.8 blocks in this series. Hibbert was selected as an [[List of NBA All-Stars|All-Star]] reserve for the East in [[2014 NBA All-Star Game|2014]]. He played 12 minutes and tallied eight points on 4–5 shooting. At the end of the season, Hibbert finished second in the [[NBA Defensive Player of the Year Award|Defensive Player of the Year]] voting with 166 out of the 1125, losing to [[Joakim Noah]], who had 555 of the points. Hibbert averaged 2.2 blocks per game. During the [[2014 NBA playoffs]], Hibbert went scoreless in games 5 and 6 of the Pacers' first round match against the eighth seed, [[Atlanta Hawks]]. Hibbert was the second All-Star to ever go scoreless in consecutive games in the playoffs, the first being [[Jim King (basketball, born 1941)|Jim King]] in 1968.{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2048766-roy-hibbert-ties-46-year-old-record-for-scoreless-playoff-games-by-all-star|title=Roy Hibbert Ties 46-Year-Old Record for Scoreless Playoff Games by All-Star|first=Stephen|last=Babb|website=Bleacher Report}} Hibbert would also have scoreless games in Game 1 of the semifinals (against the [[Washington Wizards]]) and in Game 4 of the conference finals (against the Miami Heat). By the end of the 2014 postseason, Hibbert had four scoreless postseason games, setting an NBA record for most scoreless NBA postseason games by a current All-Star. Hibbert's season ended in the Eastern Conference Finals as the Pacers were eliminated by the [[Miami Heat]] in six games, adding history to the Heat–Pacers rivalry. On June 29, 2015, Hibbert exercised his player option with the Pacers for the [[2015–16 Indiana Pacers season|2015–16 season]]. ===Los Angeles Lakers (2015–2016)=== [[File:Roy Hibbert with Lakers (2) (cropped).jpg|thumb|Hibbert with the [[Los Angeles]] Lakers in December 2015]] On July 9, 2015, Hibbert was traded to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in exchange for a second-round pick in the [[2019 NBA draft]] ([[Eric Paschall]]), which Indiana turned into [[Rakeem Christmas]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/150709_royHibbert|title=Lakers Acquire Roy Hibbert|work=NBA.com|date=July 9, 2015|access-date=July 9, 2015}} He made his debut for the Lakers in their season opener on October 28, 2015, recording 12 points and 10 rebounds in a 112–111 loss to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151028/MINLAL/gameinfo.html|title=Wolves edge Lakers 112–111 in first game since Flip's death|work=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2015|access-date=October 29, 2015}} Hibbert started in 81 of 82 games, also playing alongside [[Kobe Bryant]] in his last [[2015–16 NBA season|NBA season]]. ===Charlotte Hornets (2016–2017)=== On July 7, 2016, Hibbert signed with the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/press-releases/charlotte-hornets-sign-center-roy-hibbert|title=Charlotte Hornets Sign Center Roy Hibbert|work=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2016|access-date=July 7, 2016}} He made his debut for the Hornets in their season opener on October 26, 2016, recording 15 points and nine rebounds in a 107–96 win over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899384|title=Kidd-Gilchrist, Hibbert help Hornets beat Bucks 107–96|work=ESPN.com|date=October 26, 2016|access-date=October 27, 2016}} On January 18, 2017, Hibbert scored a season-high 16 points on 7-of-8 shooting in a 107–85 win over the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900050|title=Walker, Hibbert lead Hornets past Blazers 107–85|work=ESPN.com|date=January 18, 2017|access-date=January 19, 2017}} On the [[Charlotte Hornets|Hornets]], he played alongside 4x [[List of NBA All-Stars|NBA All-Star]] [[Kemba Walker]]. ===Denver Nuggets (2017)=== On February 2, 2017, Hibbert was traded, along with [[Spencer Hawes]], to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in exchange for former Pacers teammate [[Miles Plumlee]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-acquire-spencer-hawes-and-roy-hibbert-charlotte|title=Bucks Acquire Spencer Hawes and Roy Hibbert from Charlotte|work=NBA.com|date=February 2, 2017|access-date=February 2, 2017}} However, before appearing in a game for the Bucks, he was traded again, this time to the [[Denver Nuggets]] on February 23, in exchange for a protected 2019 second-round draft pick.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/roy-hibbert-022317|title=Nuggets Acquire Center Roy Hibbert|work=NBA.com|date=February 23, 2017|access-date=February 23, 2017}} The Nuggets renounced their free agent exception rights on Hibbert during the subsequent off-season, making him an [[unrestricted free agent]].{{cite web|url=http://www.spotrac.com/nba/denver-nuggets/roy-hibbert-6113/|title=Roy Hibbert|work=spotrac.com|date=July 13, 2017|access-date=January 16, 2018}} In Denver, Hibbert played with a young [[Nikola Jokić]]. On July 17, 2018, Hibbert announced his retirement.{{cite web|first=Andrew|last=Hussey|title=Former Pacer Roy Hibbert retires|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/2018/07/18/former-pacer-roy-hibbert-retires/795033002/|website=Indianapolis Star|date=July 18, 2018|access-date=August 14, 2018}} ==Coaching career== On August 9, 2019, it was reported that Hibbert was hired by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] as a player development specialist on the coaching staff.{{cite web|first=Paul|last=Hudrick|title=Sixers bring in former All-Star center Roy Hibbert ... but not to play|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/76ers/sixers-bring-former-all-star-center-roy-hibbert-not-play|date=August 9, 2019|website=nbcsports.com|access-date=August 9, 2019}} He served this role until becoming a college basketball analyst for [[CBS Sports]] in 2022. ==National team career== In the summer of 2007, Hibbert was the starting center on the U.S. team, which was composed of college players, at the [[Basketball at the 2007 Pan American Games|2007 Pan-American Games]].{{cite web|url=http://www.usab.com/mens/panamerican/mpag_2007.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140101174020/http://www.usab.com/mens/panamerican/mpag_2007.html|url-status=dead|title=Fifteenth Pan American Games — 2007|archive-date=January 1, 2014}} In 2009, he expressed an interest to play for the [[Jamaica national basketball team|Jamaica national team]].{{cite web |last1=Levy |first1=Leighton |title=Pacers' Hibbert could play for Jamaica |url=https://mobile.jamaica-gleaner.com/20090917/sports/sports8.php |website=Jamaica Gleaner |access-date=December 8, 2024 |date=September 17, 2009}} He has dual U.S. and Jamaican citizenship due to his father. He was named captain of the Jamaican team in 2010 and represented them in the [[2010 Centrobasket]].[http://sportsjamaica.com/read_article.php?id=18463 Jamaica's Hibbert working hard to reach the top] ==Personal life== In September 2014, Hibbert married his long-time girlfriend, Valerie Cooke.{{Cite web |last=Benbow |first=Dana Hunsinger |title=Indiana Pacers Roy Hibbert gets married |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/2014/09/22/indiana-pacers-roy-hibbert-gets-married/16080049/ |access-date=2025-05-04 |website=The Indianapolis Star |language=en-US}} The couple had met in college at [[Georgetown University]]. Hibbert works as a college basketball analyst for [[CBS Sports]], serving this role during the 2022–23 and 2023–24 seasons.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/roy-hibbert-returns-to-indy-im-always-going-to-be-a-pacer#|title=Roy Hibbert Returns to Indy: "I'm Always Going to be a Pacer"|date=October 26, 2023|website=NBA.com}} As of 2024, Hibbert lives in Maryland with his wife and four children. In 2023, Hibbert started his own [[YouTube]] channel, analyzing and reacting to news around the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]].{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/@RoyHibbertYT/featured|title=RoyHibbertYT|date=August 21, 2023|website=YouTube.com}} In popular media, Hibbert appeared as a guest star playing himself on three episodes of the comedy series ''[[Parks and Recreation]]'' which aired between 2011 and 2013. He also appeared in an episode of ''[[The Eric Andre Show]]'' in 2016.{{cite web|url=https://www.adultswim.com/videos/the-eric-andre-show/roy-hibbert-interview|title=Roy Hibbert Interview: Is this basketball?|date=September 30, 2016|website=AdultSwim.com}} Recently, Hibbert was interviewed by [[ESPN]] in 2020 to discuss the decline of the [[Center (basketball)|"Big Man"]] in the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]],{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ePVznd_vhp8|title=Roy Hibbert's Exclusive ESPN Interview on the Decline of the Big Man in the NBA|date=January 20, 2020|website=YouTube.com}} and again in 2023 by the [[Indiana Pacers|Pacers]] to celebrate the 10th anniversary of his famous block against [[Carmelo Anthony]] in the [[2013 NBA playoffs]].{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JWlyNboZLtc|title=The Sideline Guys Podcast: Roy Hibbert Indiana Pacers|date=May 18, 2023|website=YouTube.com}} During the post-game press conference after Game 6 of the 2013 Eastern Conference Finals against the [[Miami Heat]], Hibbert used the term "[[no homo]]" and later was fined $75,000 by the NBA for the remark.{{cite web|title=Roy Hibbert fined, apologizes for slur|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/playoffs/2013/story/_/id/9334504/2013-nba-playoffs-roy-hibbert-indiana-pacers-apologizes-postgame-gay-slur|publisher=ESPN|access-date=June 2, 2013|date=June 2, 2013}} Hibbert apologized for his comments in a statement released by the [[Indiana Pacers|Pacers]]: "I am apologizing for insensitive remarks made during the post-game press conference after our victory over Miami Saturday night", he said. "They were disrespectful and offensive and not a reflection of my personal views. I used a slang term that is not appropriate in any setting, private or public, and the language I used definitely has no place in a public forum, especially over live television. I apologize to those who I have offended, to our fans and to the Pacers' organization."{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/playoffs/2013/story/_/id/9334504/2013-nba-playoffs-roy-hibbert-indiana-pacers-apologizes-postgame-gay-slur|title=Hibbert fined $75,000 for postgame gay slur|date=June 2, 2013|website=ESPN.com}} ==NBA career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===Regular season=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"|{{nbay|2008}} | style="text-align:left;"|[[2008–09 Indiana Pacers season|Indiana]] | 69 || 42 || 14.4 || .471 || {{sort|-|—}} || .667 || 3.5 || .7 || .3 || 1.1 || 7.1 |- | style="text-align:left;"|{{nbay|2009}} | style="text-align:left;"|[[2009–10 Indiana Pacers season|Indiana]] | '''81''' || 69 || 25.1 || .495 || '''.500''' || .754 || 5.7 || '''2.0''' || .4 || 1.6 || 11.7 |- | style="text-align:left;"|{{nbay|2010}} | style="text-align:left;"|[[2010–11 Indiana Pacers season|Indiana]] | '''81''' || 80 || 27.7 || .461 || .000 || .745 || 7.5 || '''2.0''' || .4 || 1.8 || 12.7 |- | style="text-align:left;"|{{nbay|2011}} | style="text-align:left;"|[[2011–12 Indiana Pacers season|Indiana]] | 65 || 65 || '''29.8''' || .497 || .000 || .711 || '''8.8''' || 1.7 || '''.5''' || 2.0 || '''12.8''' |- | style="text-align:left;"|{{nbay|2012}} | style="text-align:left;"|[[2012–13 Indiana Pacers season|Indiana]] | 79 || 79 || 28.7 || .448 || .250 || .741 || 8.3 || 1.4 || '''.5''' || '''2.6''' || 11.9 |- | style="text-align:left;"|{{nbay|2013}} | style="text-align:left;"|[[2013–14 Indiana Pacers season|Indiana]] | '''81''' || '''81''' || 29.7 || .439 || .400 || .770 || 6.6 || 1.1 || .4 || 2.2 || 10.8 |- | style="text-align:left;"|{{nbay|2014}} | style="text-align:left;"|[[2014–15 Indiana Pacers season|Indiana]] | 76 || 76 || 25.3 || .446 || .000 || '''.824''' || 7.1 || 1.1 || .2 || 1.6 || 10.6 |- | style="text-align:left;"|{{nbay|2015}} | style="text-align:left;"|[[2015–16 Los Angeles Lakers season|L.A.
